scenario.name: CircleCI Official Security Alert, GitHub Security & CISA — CircleCI CI/CD Supply Chain Breach: Engineer macOS Infostealer, 2FA Session Theft & Customer Vault Exfiltration
scenario.overview: Imagine a master build-automation vault that safeguards secret keys for thousands of software companies. An intruder infects a single senior engineer laptop with a silent pocket-picking program that lifts an already-stamped two-factor entry pass straight from the browser, replays that active pass from abroad to copy both the encrypted customer lockboxes and the live decoding key from the vault control room, and unlocks thousands of customer cloud and code keys offline. In this scenario (T1539, CircleCI Official Security Alert, GitHub Security & CISA, CircleCI CI/CD Supply Chain Breach: Engineer macOS Infostealer, 2FA Session Theft & Customer Vault Exfiltration), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: engineer macOS Infostealer Infection, then session Replay from Foreign IP, Production, then offline Decryption of Customer CI/CD Secrets. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Engineer macOS Infostealer Infection, then Session Replay from Foreign IP, Production, then Offline Decryption of Customer CI/CD Secrets. Primary detection pivots on EDR Event 1 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Engineer macOS Infostealer Infection & 2FA-Backed Browser Session Cookie Theft
stages.subtitle: Initial Access & Credential Access (T1539 - Steal Web Session Cookie / T1555.003)
stages.description: After a senior engineer installs a trojanized helper tool on a work laptop, a quiet stealer slips inside the browser drawer and copies an already-verified security wristband, skipping the two-factor badge gate entirely because the wristband already carries its fresh stamp. stages.title: Stage 2: Session Replay from Foreign IP, Production Database Access & KMS Key Extraction
stages.subtitle: Privilege Escalation & Collection (T1550.004 - Web Session Cookie / T1552)
stages.description: Wearing the stolen wristband from an overseas relay booth, the intruder walks straight into the central vault control room, wheels out copies of the encrypted customer secret ledgers, and separately grabs the live master decoding key sitting in the vault engine room. Replaying the stolen engineer session token from a remote proxy IP, the attacker accesses privileged internal CircleCI production hosts, extracts database encryption keys from the running runtime environment, and dumps customer project databases containing encrypted environment variables and OAuth tokens (logged in CloudTrail Event 200 with SessionAnomaly=SSO session cookie replayed from new ASN/IP, CompromisedAssets=Production Datastores + Runtime Encryption Keys so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Replay SSO Cookie -> Access production bastion -> Dump customer context/project tables & KMS runtime decryption keys (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Replay SSO Cookie -> Access production bastion -> Dump customer context/project tables & KMS so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1550.004 during "Session Replay from Foreign IP, Production Database Access & KMS Key Extraction" , Replaying the stolen engineer session token from a remote proxy IP, the attacker accesses privileged internal CircleCI production hosts, extracts database encryption keys from the running runtime environment, and dumps customer project databases containing encrypted environment variables and OAuth tokens while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ aws-kms / ⇠#2 ACK 200) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Engineer macOS Laptop (Infostealer Malware)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Customer CI/CD Secrets, SSH Keys & GitHub Tokens).

keySpecs.value: Replay SSO Cookie -> Access production bastion -> Dump customer context/project tables & KMS runtime decryption keys
Require step-up hardware FIDO2 re-authentication for every production bastion login or KMS decryption key access regardless of active SSO cookie state.
Privilege Escalation & Collection (T1550.004 - Web Session Cookie / T1552)

stages.title: Stage 3: Offline Decryption of Customer CI/CD Secrets & Downstream GitHub / AWS Token Replay
stages.subtitle: Lateral Movement & Impact (T1552.001 - Credentials In Files / T1199 - Trusted Relationship)
stages.description: Safe inside their own hideout, the intruder pairs the stolen master decoding key with the copied ledgers to crack open customer build secrets offline, then replays those freshly uncovered GitHub and cloud keys across downstream company estates. Combining the exfiltrated database dumps with the stolen runtime encryption keys, the attacker decrypts customer CI/CD environment variables (AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, NPM_TOKEN, SSH deploy keys, and GitHub OAuth tokens) offline and attempts unauthorized git clone and aws sts get-caller-identity calls against customer repositories and cloud accounts (logged in CloudTrail Event 1 with ExfiltratedSecrets=Customer Environment Variables, SSH Deploy Keys, GitHub OAuth Tokens, ArchitecturalDefense=Short-lived OIDC Federated Tokens instead of static CI secrets so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Offline AES-GCM Decryption of Customer Project Contexts -> Recover AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, GITHUB_TOKEN, SSH Private Keys (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Offline AES-GCM Decryption of Customer Project Contexts -> Recover AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, GITHUB so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1552.001 during "Offline Decryption of Customer CI/CD Secrets & Downstream GitHub / AWS Token Replay" , Combining the exfiltrated database dumps with the stolen runtime encryption keys, the attacker decrypts customer CI/CD environment variables , AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, NPM_TOKEN, SSH deploy keys, and GitHub OAuth tokens offline and attempts unauthorized git clone and aws sts get-caller-identity calls against customer repositories and cloud accounts while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact git clone https://x-access-token:<stolen_oauth>@github.com/customer-org/private-repo.git runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , git clone https://x-access-token:<stolen_oauth>@github.com/customer-org/private-repo.git via so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1552.001 during "Offline Decryption of Customer CI/CD Secrets & Downstream GitHub / AWS Token Replay" , Combining the exfiltrated database dumps with the stolen runtime encryption keys, the attacker decrypts customer CI/CD environment variables , AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, NPM_TOKEN, SSH deploy keys, and GitHub OAuth tokens offline and attempts unauthorized git clone and aws sts get-caller-identity calls against customer repositories and cloud accounts while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ github-audit / ⇠#3 ACK 1) from Node ③ (#3 Engineer macOS Laptop (Infostealer Malware)) to Node ④ (#4 CircleCI Production Bastion & KMS Key Service), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Customer CI/CD Secrets, SSH Keys & GitHub Tokens).

steps.simpleExplanation: Combining the exfiltrated database dumps with the stolen runtime encryption keys, the attacker decrypts customer CI/CD environment variables (AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, NPM_TOKEN, SSH deploy keys, and GitHub OAuth tokens) offline and attempts unauthorized git clone and aws sts get-caller-identity calls against customer repositories and cloud accounts (logged in CloudTrail Event 1 with ExfiltratedSecrets=Customer Environment Variables, SSH Deploy Keys, GitHub OAuth Tokens, ArchitecturalDefense=Short-lived OIDC Federated Tokens instead of static CI secrets so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).

steps.diagramAlignment: On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 across the topology from Threat Actor , Stolen macOS SSO Session Cookie and Engineer macOS Laptop , Infostealer Malware toward CircleCI Production Bastion & KMS Key Service and CircleCI / GitHub OAuth & AWS CloudTrail Sensor.
steps.detectionAndEvidence: Documented in CloudTrail Event 1 (recording ExfiltratedSecrets=Customer Environment Variables, SSH Deploy Keys, GitHub OAuth Tokens, ArchitecturalDefense=Short-lived OIDC Federated Tokens instead of static CI secrets under T1552.001): Replace long-lived static AWS/GCP secrets in CI/CD pipelines with short-lived OpenID Connect (OIDC) federated tokens (sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity) that expire immediately after each build job.
